questions.question: A box measures 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. Find its volume, then the volume when one dimension is doubled, when two are doubled and when all three are doubled. State the multiplier each time and explain the pattern.
questions.expected_answer: Original 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³. One doubled, for example 8 × 3 × 2 = 48 cm³, times 2. Two doubled, 8 × 6 × 2 = 96 cm³, times 4. All three doubled, 8 × 6 × 4 = 192 cm³, times 8. Volume is a product of three dimensions, so each doubled dimension multiplies the product by another 2: 2, 2 × 2 = 4, 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

questions.question: A cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 5 cm. Find its volume, and the volume when the height is doubled, when the radius is doubled, and when both are doubled. Explain why doubling the radius has a bigger effect than doubling the height.
questions.expected_answer: Original π × 2² × 5 = 20π ≈ 62.83 cm³. Height doubled: π × 4 × 10 = 40π ≈ 125.66 cm³, times 2. Radius doubled: π × 4² × 5 = 80π ≈ 251.33 cm³, times 4. Both doubled: π × 16 × 10 = 160π ≈ 502.65 cm³, times 8. The radius appears squared in πr²h because it sets the width of the circular base in both directions, so doubling it multiplies the base area, and the volume, by 2² = 4, while the height appears once and gives a factor of 2.

questions.question: Every dimension of a cube of side 5 cm is doubled. Compare the new volume and surface area with the old, then state the general rule for a scale factor k and use it to find the scale factor for a container in the same shape that holds 27 times as much.
questions.expected_answer: Old volume 5³ = 125 cm³, new 10³ = 1 000 cm³, times 8. Old surface area 6 × 25 = 150 cm², new 6 × 100 = 600 cm², times 4. For scale factor k: lengths × k, areas × k², volumes × k³. Holding 27 times as much means k³ = 27, so k is the cube root of 27, which is 3: every length is tripled.
